## Sample statistics

```{python}
#| include: false
import random
import statistics

random.seed(1)
x = [random.gauss(3.2, 0.4) for _ in range(100)]
```

A hundred samples were collected for analysis.

```{python}
round(statistics.mean(x), 3), round(statistics.stdev(x), 3)
```

Python has no inline-expression syntax equivalent to R's `` `r ...` ``, so a
cell prints the shortcode text directly. `#| output: asis` tells Quarto to
treat the cell's printed output as markdown (so the shortcode gets expanded)
rather than as a literal code-output block:

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
print(f"The mean of this sample is {{{{< cloze-numerical {statistics.mean(x):f} tolerance=0.5 >}}}}.")
```
